newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas centres on May in busier trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas centres on May in busier trade.

text.p: The IPE natural gas contract saw 215 lots traded on Monday, far higher than normally seen at the start of the week, with most trade concentrated in front month May at higher prices.
May saw 80 deals done in several trades, with the last done at 10.30 pence a therm after the market had opened at 10.20 pence. The contract had settled on Friday at 10.225 pence a therm.

Further out every month from June to October traded 25 lots, in each case represented by a single trade. Prices in this period were mixed, with June, July and September all rising while August and October were slightly off. April 1998 also traded a single lot at 12.25 pence, down 0.06 pence form Friday.
A futures broker said much of the trade had been done by the small number of traders with their own screens, allowing them to trade directly.

He added that there were rumours that there may have been some short term production problems at one or two offshore fields which could have led to the interest in the front month, but no details emerged.
